value.a: NOT a collision with the tester's network seal, though it is the nearest neighbour: one keeps a proof off the network, this keeps it out of the live instance root. Same owner, same discipline, different resource. The distinction belongs on the tester's charter — instance-space is the seal's second resource — and the seal's inside-probe rule crosses to it unchanged.

NOT a collision with address.py's no-touch-disk bound, and the reason is load-bearing: this seam changes the ENVIRONMENT address.py resolves in, and adds no read, no import and no branch to the module. A build that put the dial inside address.py would satisfy this ticket and break that one.

The parent's coverage number (trails-on-disk against components-that-emit) will DROP when the fixtures stop being written. That is the number becoming honest rather than regressing, and the parent's watchme already carries measured counts rather than a pass word precisely so a reader can tell which.

SETTLED BY AKIEN 2026-08-18, the same hour this was cast, and it replaces the out-of-scope clause this ticket filed. He asked the only question that mattered: 'what do we need them for? if you can't come up with a reason to keep them, not a well maybe, then we just delete them.' MEASURED IN ANSWER: the entire ~/.cairn/logs tree spanned SEVENTEEN MINUTES — 18:33:27 to 18:51:26 — across every one of its eight trails, which is exactly the window of the session's two corpus runs. So it was not 440 fixtures among 2,080 real records, as CC had reported an hour earlier; it was 2,080 records of proof exhaust, and the real-looking pointers were proofs exercising real trouble ids. Nothing read the tree. No keep-reason survived, so the eight trails went through bin/cmd/trash (recoverable, 30 days). THE LAW 7 QUESTION THE CAST RAISED DISSOLVED rather than being answered: a record of what a proof staged is not a record of truth about the world, and treating it as one is what made deleting it feel like it needed a ruling.

MEASURED IN THE SAME ACT and NOT deleted: the only real diagnostic history in instance-space lives at the OLD address — ~/.cairn/devices/bus/0/diagnostics.jsonl (312 records) and ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/0/diagnostics.jsonl (168 records), spanning 2026-08-12 to 2026-08-18, written by the live ground loop. Six days of genuine operational record, untouched, and it is what makes the 17-minute tree's emptiness legible: the history everyone assumed was accumulating was accumulating somewhere else.

THE BUILD IS DONE AND THE VOYAGE CANNOT CROSS, and the cursor stands at [TICKETME] for that reason rather than by neglect. Measured 2026-08-18: the seal is built (cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py + device.py), proven green (cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_instance_seal.py, 8 teeth + a byte witness, run four times), the probe is berthed and armed (cairn/devices/tester/probes/a_proof_cannot_seed_the_tree_it_reads.py), the charter carries it, and all of it is committed at 9163ffc. The BUILDME crossing was then attempted through the chokepoint and REFUSED, verbatim: "[buildme_rides_the_chart] no berthed chart chain claims ticket 'a-proof-cannot-seed-the-tree-it-reads' — the build has no charted course". Nothing was journaled. THE DOOR IS RIGHT: CC built from the conversation, across a context boundary, without firing /chart, which is the exact step-skipping buildme-rides-the-chart was built to catch — and it caught it.

THE DISPOSITION IS DELIBERATELY *NOT* TO BACKFILL THE CHART, and this is the part worth reading in a year. A chart chain authored after the build would produce validate criteria written by someone who already knows what was built, and step 6 of /sail would then answer those criteria with the instruments that build shipped. That is a hollow pass wearing the gate's own costume — the shape Law 8 refuses — and it would leave the trees a memory of a course that never steered anything. Manufacturing the record a door demands is worse than the missing record, because the missing record is legible and the manufactured one is not. So the cursor stays where the physics put it, the code stands proven in git, and the contradiction is written here rather than smoothed over (Law 5: the thing and the story of the thing may live in two roots; what they may never do is contradict each other — this note is what keeps them from it).

WHAT THE SEAL ACTUALLY BOUGHT, measured after a full corpus run under it (127 proofs, 125 green, 2 red, both pre-existing): ~/.cairn/logs now holds ONE device trail — the tester's, 161 records spanning the 14 minutes it was actually running — against 2,080 records across EIGHT devices before, none of which were running. A byte witness over the whole run recorded 0 files added to live instance-space; the only movement was the tester's own trail (it runs unsealed in the parent process and logs that it ran, which is a real crossing) and two daemon status files. The ticket's falsifier said DONE when a full run leaves the tree BYTE-IDENTICAL, and that bar is measurably wrong by one term: the tester is itself a device, so a corpus run must move the tester's trail or the tester stopped logging. The honest bar, and the one the proof asserts, is that no SUBJECT write reaches the host — asked by name against the paths the seal itself recorded.

OWED, and named so it is not rediscovered: this ticket cannot reach PROVED without a ruling from Akien on how a build that ran ahead of its chart is landed. Two routes exist and both are his, not CC's — an exemption at the door for a build whose proofs and probe already stand, or a re-run of the work under a real chart. CC's own reading, offered and not acted on: neither is obviously right, and the general question (what the corpus does with a proven seam whose voyage was skipped) outlives this ticket.
